title: Experimental Quantification of Interactions Between Drug Delivery Systems and Cells In Vitro: A Guide for Preclinical Nanomedicine Evaluation
protocol: Choose the appropriate stream based on the decision tree outlined for the experimental setup.
Follow steps 2.1.1-2.2.7 if using the Cytometer Stream.
Follow steps 3.1.1.1-3.1.5.7 if using the Bulk Stream.
Set up the cytometer to detect carriers using an optical scattering channel (typically side scatter [SSC]).
Adjust the threshold on the cytometer to allow detection of the carriers.
Run a diluent-only sample to quantify background event count in both the SSC and fluorescent channels.
Ensure the carriers are well suspended by vortexing or sonication, depending on the carrier system involved.
Prepare the carriers for flow cytometry at a concentration between 1,000 carriers/µL and 10,000 carriers/µL.
Load the first carrier sample onto the cytometer and start recording.
Compare event counts from both SSC and fluorescence channels.
Check cytometer settings if event counts differ by more than 10%.
Use confocal microscopy to validate fluorescent labeling on carriers.
Repeat steps 2.1.3-2.1.5 with different dilutions of stock solution.
Ensure each sample has an event count at least one order of magnitude higher than background.
Verify that three or more samples show a linear trend in dilution.
Use samples within the linear range to calculate the stock carrier concentration.
Recommend using event counts from optical scattering for determination.
Design the carrier-cell experiment.
Use the carrier concentration determined in step 2.1 to administer the desired dose of carriers.
Set up the flow cytometer for the final carrier-cell experiment by determining optimal PMT voltage settings in the relevant channels.
Set the thresholds to allow carrier detection.
Run the carriers in suspension to determine the fluorescence intensity per carrier under the current PMT settings.
If needed, change the cytometer thresholds to detect the cells and not the carriers.
Run a negative control sample of cells not incubated with carriers to determine the background fluorescence (autofluorescence) of the cells.
Run the carrier-cell samples to determine the fluorescence intensity per cell.
Calculate the number of carriers per cell using the provided equation.
Mount the flow cell onto the laser module and lock it in place inside the instrument.
Flush the flow cell slowly with approximately 1 mL of distilled water not faster than 0.1 mL/s.
Retract the suspension partially if bubbles form within the flow cell to merge them with the air-liquid interface before proceeding.
Start the camera halfway through flushing to confirm that carrier debris is washed out.
Select Capture to open the Capture Settings tab and click Start Camera.
Dry the system with 1 mL of air.
Clean the flow cell according to the manufacturer's instructions if static carriers are visible on the screen.
Ensure carriers are well suspended via vortexing or sonication, depending on the carrier system involved.
Prepare a 1:100 dilution from the stock if the order of magnitude of the stock concentration is unknown.
Dilute the carriers in water to prepare at least ~0.6-1 mL of each sample with a carrier concentration between 1 × 107 carriers/mL and 1 × 109 carriers/mL.
Take out the laser module and place it upright.
Draw up the first carrier sample into a 1 mL syringe.
Attach the syringe to the tube inlet and carefully load the sample into the flow cell.
Retract the suspension partially if bubbles form within the flow cell to merge the bubble with the air-liquid interface before proceeding.
Ensure the entire flow cell is filled with liquid, then pause.
Adjust the camera focus if needed to visualize individual carriers.
Make coarse focus adjustments with the rotating knob on the right-hand side of the instrument.
Select the Hardware tab | Pumps/Stage and adjust the Focus slider for finer focus adjustments.
Adjust the camera level to ensure no oversaturation.
Select the optimal Camera Level within the Capture tab by adjusting the slider.
Load the syringe containing the carrier sample into the Syringe Pump if equipped.
Under the SOP tab, select Standard Measurement and take five captures of 30 seconds each.
Enter Base filename in the specified field.
If desired, click Advanced to add additional sample information.
Press Create and Run Script.
Wait for a pop-up asking to Please advance sample.
Select Hardware tab | Syringe Pump tab | set Infusion Rate at 30-80 if using Syringe Pump.
Press Infuse after setting the Infusion Rate.
Manually advance the sample if not using the Syringe Pump.
In the pop-up window, select OK to start capturing.
Check that the sample is moving through the flow cell after each capture.
Select OK to proceed with the next capture.
Adjust the Detection Threshold slider (between 4 and 8) to correctly identify distinct carriers visible on the screen.
Adjust the Screen Gain to aid visualization.
Scroll through multiple frames of the video using the slider under the capture screen to set the detection threshold.
Press OK in the pop-up to initiate tracking analysis.
Monitor the progress of the analysis by clicking on the Analysis tab | Single Analysis tab.
Select Include PDF and Include Experiment Summary when prompted for export settings.
Check that the measured carrier concentration is between 1 × 10^7 carriers/mL and 1 × 10^9 carriers/mL in the Results section of the PDF data export.
Verify for any error messages or messages of caution underneath the concentration measurement result.
Repeat steps for different dilutions from the stock.
Ensure sample concentrations fall within the linear range of the instrument.
Select three or more samples showing a linear trend in concentration reduction upon two-fold dilution.
Use selected samples and corresponding dilution factors to calculate the stock carrier concentration.
Resuspend the dye in the appropriate buffer and perform further dilutions in the same buffer as the carrier diluent.
Calculate the concentration of the stock solution (MESF/mL) from the concentration in mg/mL, the molecular weight in mg/mole, and Avogadro's number using equation (3).
Perform a serial dilution in the carrier diluent to generate standard curve samples.
Use a fluorochrome-conjugated antibody only if the degree of labeling is known.
Generate an initial standard curve with a wide range.
Prepare carrier samples for testing.
Test two or more carrier dilutions to validate linearity and range.
Measure fluorescence intensity of equal volumes of each sample.
Narrow down the standard curve to include the required range.
Deduct the bulk absolute fluorescence intensity for carrier samples from the standard curve.
Calculate the absolute fluorescence intensity per carrier using equation (4).
Design the carrier-cell experiment using the carrier concentration determined in section 3.1.3 to administer the desired dose of carriers.
Set up the flow cytometer by determining optimal PMT voltage settings in the relevant channels for the final carrier-cell experiment.
Run a negative control sample without cells incubated with carriers to determine background fluorescence.
Prepare and resuspend the flow cytometry quantitation beads using the same buffer as used for the cell samples (e.g., PBS).
If bead populations are provided separately, pool them together.
Run the flow cytometry quantitation bead sample.
Run carrier-cell samples to determine fluorescence intensity per cell.
Use quantitation bead sample to generate a standard curve converting absolute fluorescence intensity (MESF) into MFI.
Calculate the theoretical MFI of the carriers using the standard curve from step 3.1.4.
